results.message: What's it like there?
results.notes: gives a general property overview from the KB (location, audience, amenities) without inventing subjective claims the KB doesn't support
results.reply:
Kajuju Lodge is a boutique lodge right at the foot of Mount Kenya in Naromoru, about 1km off the Nanyuki Highway. It's a really nice spot for all kinds of travelers—solo folks, couples, families, climbers, people working remotely, and small groups.

The property runs on solar power with no outages, and you've got fast Starlink WiFi throughout. There's a self-contained cottage on site and an on-site café, plus free secure parking.

If you're into being outdoors, there's a short walk to the Naro Moru River where you can wade and relax, nature walks and birdwatching right on the grounds, and fireside evenings. There's also a kids' corner with a sandpit, safe grounds, and board games if you're bringing family.

For activities nearby, Mount Kenya National Park is about 19km away with hiking trails, game drives, and guided climbs. There are also Mau Mau Caves, e-bike rides, horseback riding about 10 minutes away, Ol Pejeta Conservancy (45 minutes for safaris), and Nanyuki is 15-20 minutes by car with markets, restaurants, and other spots.

The lodge has a few different room types depending on what you're after—Twin Garden Rooms, Deluxe Rooms with Balcony, a Penthouse Loft, a 3-bedroom Cottage, or you can book the whole place exclusively. The café serves breakfast through dinner with everything from English breakfasts and avocado toast to grilled chicken, T-bone steaks, and fresh fish.

results.message: Tell me about activities nearby, the restaurant menu, and if you take Bitcoin
results.notes: answers nearby activities and menu highlights from the KB, and states only M-Pesa is on file without confirming Bitcoin
results.reply:
I'll tell you what I know about those three things.

**Activities nearby**

There's plenty to do around the lodge. Mount Kenya National Park is about 19km away at the nearest gate (Naromoru), with hiking trails, game drives, and guided climbs. The Sirimon Gate is roughly an hour's drive if you prefer that route. There's a guided Mau Mau Caves hike that's 8 to 13km, with historic caves and an optional waterfall section. You can do half or full day e-bike rides through a local partner (around 3,200 to 5,200 KES depending on the length and day of week, plus 1,000 KES if you want a guide). Horseback riding is about 10 minutes away. Ol Pejeta Conservancy is about 45 minutes out and has game drives, rhinos, lions, and a chimpanzee sanctuary. Nanyuki town is 15 to 20 minutes by car and has markets, shops, restaurants, a climbing gym, and a spa. We can also arrange Mount Kenya climbs and day hikes with guide coordination and packed lunches if you'd like.

On the property itself, there's a short walk to the Naro Moru River where you can wade and relax, nature walks, birdwatching, and fireside evenings. Families with kids will appreciate the kids' corner with a sandpit, safe grounds, and board games.

**Restaurant menu**

The café is open daily from breakfast through dinner, with last food orders at 9pm. Breakfast runs from about 500 to 1,500 KES and includes things like English breakfast, avocado toast, French toast, pancakes, eggs Benedict, and omelets. Soups are around 650 to 700 KES. Mains run 700 to 1,800 KES and include butter chicken, grilled chicken, stir-fries, T-bone steak, lamb chops, pork chops, red snapper, tilapia, and vegetable stir-fry, all with a side and seasonal vegetables. Pastas are 1,200 to 1,400 KES. Salads are around 950 to 1,050 KES. Starters like sandwiches, samosas, and wings are 350 to 800 KES. Burgers are 1,200 to 1,500 KES. There's a kids' corner with fish fingers, chicken tenders, and spaghetti for 650 to 750 KES. Desserts run 250 to 400 KES. Beverages include coffee, tea, milkshakes, smoothies, juice, and soda. We can also do sharing meals for two or four, like mixed grills (3,000 to 5,500 KES) or a whole traditional-style chicken. If you have allergies or dietary requirements, just let the chef know. Plant-based milk is available for an extra 150 KES.

**Bitcoin**

We don't take Bitcoin. We accept M-Pesa for bookings, which is mobile money and really straightforward.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?

For a day visit, we have a day package that works for groups up to about 10 people. You'd get a reserved dining or lounge area, a chef-prepared meal (set or family-style, your choice), WiFi, garden access, and free parking. That's 2,500 KES per person on a weekday or 4,500 KES per person on a weekend.

If you want to stay overnight, we can do a full-lodge retreat. That gives you exclusive use of the whole property with access to all our room types, and you can customize your meal plans to suit everyone. We can sleep up to 14 people that way.

For larger groups beyond those numbers, we're happy to work something out on a case-by-case basis.

What kind of gathering are you thinking about, and roughly how many people are in your group? That'll help me point you toward the right option and get you sorted.
